Abstract
               
                  Summary
                  Over the last two decades, we have observed an exponential increase in the number of generated array or sequencing-based transcriptomic profiles. Reverse engineering of biological networks from high-throughput gene expression profiles has been one of the grand challenges in systems biology. The Algorithm for the Reconstruction of Accurate Cellular Networks (ARACNe) represents one of the most effective and widely-used tools to address this challenge. However, existing ARACNe implementations do not efficiently process big input data with thousands of samples. Here we present an improved implementation of the algorithm, SJARACNe, to solve this big data problem, based on sophisticated software engineering. The new scalable SJARACNe package achieves a dramatic improvement in computational performance in both time and memory usage and implements new features while preserving the network inference accuracy of the original algorithm. Given that large-sampled transcriptomic data is increasingly available and ARACNe is extremely demanding for network reconstruction, the scalable SJARACNe will allow even researchers with modest computational resources to efficiently construct complex regulatory and signaling networks from thousands of gene expression profiles.
               
               
                  Availability and implementation
                  SJARACNe is implemented in C++ (computational core) and Python (pipelining scripting wrapper, ≥3.6.1). It is freely available at https://github.com/jyyulab/SJARACNe.
               
               
                  Supplementary information
                  Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

Abstract

Summary
Over the past twenty years, generated array- and sequencing-based transcriptomic profiles have grown exponentially. Reconstructing biological networks from high-throughput gene expression data has long been a major challenge in systems biology. The Algorithm for the Reconstruction of Accurate Cellular Networks (ARACNe) is among the most effective and widely used methods for tackling this problem. Yet current ARACNe implementations are not efficient when handling large input datasets with thousands of samples. To address this big-data issue, we introduce SJARACNe, an enhanced implementation of the algorithm built through advanced software engineering. The scalable SJARACNe package delivers major gains in computational speed and memory use, while adding new features and maintaining the network-inference accuracy of the original method. As large-sample transcriptomic datasets become more widely available and ARACNe remains highly demanding for network reconstruction, scalable SJARACNe will enable even researchers with modest computational resources to efficiently build complex regulatory and signaling networks from thousands of gene expression profiles.

Availability and implementation
SJARACNe is implemented in C++ for the computational core and Python for the pipelining scripting wrapper (≥3.6.1). It is freely available at https://github.com/jyyulab/SJARACNe.

Supplementary information
Supplementary data are available online at Bioinformatics.
